entries.title: Dress up your penguin
changes: Instances now wear a penguin as their icon, and you can dress it up on the new Icon tab: a top hat, party hat or beanie, sunglasses or a monocle, a scarf or a bow tie, all free.
Rather have your own picture? Choose Custom image on the Icon tab.
The Cosmetics page has a Penguin wardrobe, where more accessories will be for sale.

entries.title: The penguin has news
changes: Update notices now come from the penguin, holding up a bright "!" whenever a new launcher or a new build of ABNW is ready.
Anything still on its way now has the penguin holding up a clock.

The penguin turns up all over: it gives you a thumbs-up tick, holds up a warning, brings you the news, carries your downloads, shoulders a pickaxe while you play and waits with a key when you need to sign in.
Home is now an igloo, your account is a penguin, Instances are a pair of penguins, and Cosmetics is a penguin in a top hat.
Patreon supporters have a penguin of their own, holding up a heart on a sign.

entries.title: A launcher with a world of its own
changes: The launcher has a new hand-made pixel-art look, with every button, panel and icon redrawn in ABNW's style.
The pages are now tabs along the top, with a status bar along the bottom that shows downloads, updates and what's running.

Home stands on a night-time hillside with drifting clouds and a moon, and each page sits further underground: through the soil, into the caves, down to a hidden dwarthen village and on into the deepslate.
Meet the penguin, who keeps you company next to the Play button and waves when you're about to play.
Your account now shows a little 3D head made from your own Minecraft skin, cached so it appears straight away next time.

entries.title: Offline accounts
changes: Offline accounts are now supported, but you must first sign in and authenticate an account before creating or using one.

entries.title: Cosmetics
changes: New Cosmetics page: link your Patreon to unlock supporter cosmetics. Cosmetics are purely visual and never affect gameplay, and more is coming soon.
Linking is done in your browser through Patreon, and your Minecraft account is confirmed without sharing your sign-in.

entries.title: Library and platform fixes
changes: Libraries that ship natives for only some systems now always install their main jar.
Cached files verified with SHA-256 are no longer re-downloaded on every launch.
On macOS the launcher now starts correctly with a plain java -jar.
The Linux Java installers fall back to a portable Java when sudo is not available.

entries.title: Linux support
changes: Linux now has its own download: unzip it, run ./install-java.sh if you need Java, then ./launch.sh.
The Java installer supports Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE and their derivatives, with a portable Java for everything else.
If the launcher window can't open or crashes on Wayland, it switches to X11 automatically.

entries.title: Safer downloads and accounts
changes: Every game file, library and patch is now checked against a SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash before it is used.
Sign-in tokens are kept in your system's secure storage instead of a plain file.
Cancelling an install now stops downloads straight away, and retries no longer overcount progress.
Custom Java paths are checked for the Java version the game needs.
Extra JVM arguments understand quotes, so paths with spaces work.
News and both changelogs now update from the web every time the launcher opens.
